# Tagcast 1.5.0 — A new listening experience

Tagcast 1.5.0 brings the redesigned listening workspace, fullscreen presentation and
browsing improvements to the shared desktop and browser interface.

## Now playing

- A fixed Now playing shortcut in the sidebar opens a dedicated listening page.
- Album artwork, linked artist and album information, compact format details and
  optional retro stereo meters sit alongside a focused lyrics panel.
- The play queue has artwork, a complete current-row highlight and a compact
  actions menu. Queue actions remain available beside its heading.
- Album colours provide a continuous background. Lyrics remain a temporary display;
  this page does not save online lyrics to iBroadcast or local music files.

## Fullscreen and player controls

- Choose Cover or CD independently of the Lyrics view. The cover remains upright
  while a printed disc rotates partly outside its sleeve; reflections stay still.
- Rotation pauses with playback and respects reduced motion. Ordinary Cover view
  remains available.
- Quieter selection colours, balanced lyric lines and a taller lyrics area keep the
  focus on the music. Derived text accents are checked for readable contrast.
- Both the standard controls and an optional larger transport layout are available
  in Settings. Previous and Next sit together around the playback controls.
- Sound controls are available from the sidebar footer. Like/dislike controls remain
  beside the player, with track actions available from the queue's menu.

## Browsing and remembered preferences

- Search and filtering controls stay reachable while browsing long listings.
- Changing pages scrolls back to the listing controls.
- Sorting choices are remembered separately for the supported listings.
- The local queue, selected track, Repeat and Shuffle settings can be restored after
  restarting the same browser or desktop profile. Restoration uses current library
  metadata and never starts playback automatically. Elapsed playback time is not
  restored; the selected track starts from the beginning when Play is chosen.
- Queue recovery is account-scoped and bounded to 10,000 occurrences. iBroadcast
  queue synchronization retains priority when it owns playback.

## Appearance and compatibility

- Amber joins the built-in palettes. Light, Dark and Auto remain independent of the
  selected colour palette, including in listening views.
- Thin, translucent scrollbars and less prominent listening-page buttons improve
  visual consistency. Native high-contrast fallbacks remain available.
- New controls are translated in all six supported interface languages.
- Playback uses the existing audio engine. Experimental Gapless Playback remains
  optional and off by default, with its existing supported transitions and safe
  ordinary-playback fallback. No universal sample-accuracy claim is made.

## Upgrading and platform notes

Quit older Tagcast instances before opening the update. Existing account
credentials, settings, custom themes and local preferences are retained. Choose
between the existing standard player and the larger transport in Settings.

Standalone downloads are available for macOS Apple Silicon, macOS Intel, Windows
x64 and Linux x64, each with a SHA-256 checksum. Linux requires a compatible graphical
desktop and Chromium sandbox support. Python/browser use remains available.
The illustrated PDF manual remains the labelled 1.4.0 edition; new screenshots will
follow separately.

## Code signing and privacy

The **macOS downloads are Developer ID signed and notarized by Apple**. Signatures,
stapled tickets, Gatekeeper assessment and extracted applications are checked before
publication. Windows signing through SignPath is not yet active; Windows downloads
remain unsigned. See the [Code signing policy](https://github.com/cyberdeliaAI/tagcast#code-signing-policy)
and [Privacy policy](https://github.com/cyberdeliaAI/tagcast/blob/v1.5.0/PRIVACY.md).
Tagcast does not retag existing local music files. Restoring a queue never starts
audio playback; playback begins only after an explicit action.
